newsitem.title: USA: Nu-Kote says judge rules against Hewlett-Packard.
newsitem.headline: Nu-Kote says judge rules against Hewlett-Packard.

text.p: Nu-Kote International Inc said Sunday that a federal judge in San Jose, Calif., has ruled that Hewlett-Packard Co falsely labels packages for its inkjet cartridges to make consumers believe that replacements made by other companies are incompatible with HP printers.
Federal Judge James Ware, in his ruling, enjoined Hewlett-Packard from falsely labeling its inject cartridge packaging, Nu-Kote said in a news release.

The ruling stemmed from an injunction filed in March by Nu-Kote, a Dallas-based supplier of inkjet cartridge replacements, seeking to stop Hewlett-Packard from making changes to its inkjet cartridges, claiming that it unfairly restricts competition.
Hewlett-Packard was not available to comment.
Nu-Kote is a competitor of Palo-Alto, Calif.,-based Hewlett-Packard in the resale of the HP cartridges, which Nu-Kote refills for reuse, mainly for personal computers.

According to Nu-Kote, Ware ruled that Hewlett-Packard's packaging for its two most popular inkjet cartridges is "literally false" because while the company's packaging contains cartridges for which Nu-Kote currently offers a compatible replacement, it depicts a cartridge that is not useable by Nu-Kote customers.
Nu-Kote said the judge agreed with it that Hewlett-Packard's packaging hides this fact and issued an order stating that "... HP shall be enjoined from using its false packaging."

Nu-Kote's motion for an injunction is part of ongoing litigation between the two companies. Hewlett-Packard, a computer industry giant, originally sued Nu-Kote for patent infringement and Nu-Kote has filed a counterclaim on anti-trust grounds.
Nu-Kote said the court has set a hearing for July 23 to specify exact terms of the injunction, including the effective date and termination date.
The company said that at a later time a jury trial will determine the amount of damages to be awarded.
